en: Itivuttaka 66: Tikanipāta, Dutiyavagga (The Second Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a shallow pool with a spring, the person who is like a deep pool with no spring, and the person who is like a deep pool with a spring. And how, friends, is a person like a shallow pool with a spring? Here, friends, a certain person is one whose evil unwholesome states that have arisen subside quickly. This, friends, is called a person who is like a shallow pool with a spring. And how, friends, is a person like a deep pool with no spring? Here, friends, a certain person is one whose evil unwholesome states that have arisen do not subside. This, friends, is called a person who is like a deep pool with no spring. And how, friends, is a person like a deep pool with a spring? Here, friends, a certain person is one whose evil unwholesome states that have arisen subside quickly. This, friends, is called a person who is like a deep pool with a spring. These, friends, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the Venerable Udāyī asked the Venerable Ānanda: "But how, friend Ānanda, does a person become like a shallow pool with a spring? "In this case, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. While he dwells thus, some evil unwholesome states that have arisen in him subside. Just as, friend, water that has been stirred up by a stick or a potsherd subsides quickly, so too, friend, when a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body... some evil unwholesome states that have arisen in him subside. This, friend, is how a person becomes like a shallow pool with a spring. Furthermore, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. While he dwells thus, some evil unwholesome states that have arisen in him subside. Just as, friend, water that has been stirred up by a stick or a potsherd subsides quickly, so too, friend, when a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena... some evil unwholesome states that have arisen in him subside. This too, friend, is how a person becomes like a shallow pool with a spring. And how, friend, does a person become like a deep pool with no spring? In this case, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body... feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. While he dwells thus, some evil unwholesome states that have arisen in him do not subside. This, friend, is how a person becomes like a deep pool with no spring. And how, friend, does a person become like a deep pool with a spring? In this case, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body... feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. While he dwells thus, some evil unwholesome states that have arisen in him subside. This too, friend, is how a person becomes like a deep pool with a spring. This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of purity."
Purity of body, purity of speech, and purity of mind—
these, monks, are the three purities.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
“Purity of body and purity of speech,
"Pure in mind and free from taints,
they call him the one who has abandoned everything."
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
